Western Digital Corporation Remains a Quality Value opportunity
Western Digital Remains A Quality Value Opportunity
articles.content: When I looked at WDC at 4.0x - 4.5x FCF some 14 months ago, it's price was depressed due to two primary factors in my view: The devastating floods in Thailand in October 2011 which resulted in temporary suspension of operations, as WDC's facilities there (along with those many supply chain companies to the computing and data storage industries) were forced to close, forgoing sales and incurring exceptional costs in the tidy-up; and Apple/tablet-mania swept over investors in a tidal wave-like manner, as Apple's share price marched from $570 to $700 per share between June and September 2012, as many commentators predicted it would become the first $1 trillion dollar company; WDC as a perceived PC-oriented, HDD company with little exposure to the newer solid-state drives used in most tablets, and only modest exposure to enterprise and cloud storage customers was viewed as heading towards obsolescence. Secondly, HDDs themselves have come to be viewed as a storage medium destined for obsolescence with the increased adoption of Solid State Drives ("SSDs") that use flash memory and storage technology, which offer improved performance over HDDs and which are used in tablet devices These perceptions of both WDC and data storage technology are in fact overly simplistic, flawed, and constitute a real misunderstanding of both the company and the data storage market itself, for the following reasons: Firstly, non-PC related business now accounts for 51% of WDC's revenues as of June 2013, and the company has a growing exposure to the higher margin enterprise and cloud data storage segment Secondly, WDC has and continues to develop a significant SSD offering, with 4 SSD-related acquisitions (SiliconSystems, HGST, STEC, VeloBit) since 2009 as well as a strategic investment in a pure-play, high-growth SSD business (Skyera) These acquisitions are evidence that management are transitioning the business from pure HDD to HDD and SSD, recognizing that both have a role in the continued growth of digital content and consequent storage requirements Therefore WDC is not actually just a HDD business, and indicates intelligent capital allocation by management to enhance its data storage offering, gain exposure to the high-growth SSD/tablet computing market and thereby combat any potential obsolescence risk facing traditional HDD storage. Furthermore, WDC has a consistent 10-year track record of increasing revenues, earnings and free cash flow while delivering strong returns on capital with minimal debt, to the point where it's the dominant operator in the HDD space, with a growing SSD presence In addition to the above company-specific characteristics, the general outlook for data storage business prospects appears to be quite positive: data and digital content continues to growth at an exponential rate, and is perhaps one of the great secular growth stories of our time - digital content growth and the corresponding growth in storage requirements are forecast to have a CAGR of between 30% - 50% over the next 5 - 7 years according to various industry and market reports.

articles.title: Micron Technology, Inc Is Doing a Billion-Buck Buyback. But Is This a Good Idea?
articles.content: At its current pace of cash production, Micron can afford to buy back $1 billion in stock, and then $1 billion more after that ... and then $1 billion more after that . Over that time span, the company has four times failed to generate even $1 billion in positive free cash flow -- and in one year, 2011, free cash flow actually ran negative. So what we really need to ask is, now that Micron is flush with cash, is its stock cheap enough that it should be using that cash to buy back stock?

But there are other issues Seagate and Western Digital have to deal with, such as declining prices stemming from a very competitive market and declining hard disk shipments. Storage stocks are risky The growth of data presents a big opportunity for Seagate and Western Digital, but Seagate is simply too dependent on the declining HDD market for me to have confidence it can capitalize on SSD adoption.

articles.content: Western Digital's (NASDAQ: WDC) stock was cut in half last year as cyclical headwinds in the data storage and memory chip markets throttled its growth. By end market, WD's client devices (for PCs, mobile devices, and embedded storage products) revenue fell 30% annually, its client solutions (USB drives, external drives, and flash products) revenue fell 23%, and its data center revenue tumbled 25%. Furthermore, WD reported a negative FCF of $110 million for the quarter, compared to a positive FCF of $24 million in the second quarter and $616 million in the prior year quarter.

articles.title: Is Seagate Technology an Undervalued Dividend Stock?
articles.content: Unlike its main rival, Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC), which aggressively diversified into the SSD and flash memory markets by acquiring SanDisk in 2016, Seagate still generates most of its revenue from traditional HDDs. Seagate Technology (NASDAQ: STX), one of the world's largest makers of platter-based hard disk drives (HDDs), struggled last year with slow PC sales, sluggish enterprise demand, and competition from flash-based SSDs (solid state drives), which are faster, smaller, more power-efficient, and less prone to damage than HDDs. Seagate's stock rebounded more than 20% this year on hopes for a recovery in the PC and cloud markets, but it still trades at 10 times forward earnings and pays a hefty forward dividend yield of 5%.

Western Digital Stock Upgraded: What You Need to Know
articles.content: Today, we're taking one high-profile Wall Street pick and putting it under the microscope... From May 15 -- the date President Trump signed an executive order restricting sales of U.S. technology to Chinese 5G giant Huawei -- to the end of May, shares of computer memory maker Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) lost 18% of their value. More importantly to Western Digital, Trump's announcement included a reprieve on sales of radio frequency microchips, computer memory, and other high-tech components sold by U.S. suppliers to Huawei where such sales pose "no great national security problem" to the U.S. What it means to Western Digital In an upgrade this morning, analysts at investment bank Mizuho argue that this latest twist in the trade war between America and China "effectively" takes Huawei "off the entity list" of foreign companies with which U.S. companies are unable to trade. And because this trade ban has been a major overhang for Western Digital and its business of selling computer memory to Huawei, the analyst believes that "improving visibility, a rebound in orders and upside to depressed expectations" will now benefit Western Digital stock -- which Mizuho is upgrading to buy, with a $55 price target.

articles.content: Micron Stock, Other Chip Stocks Upgraded Goldman announced a sweeping wave of upgrades that included MU’s rival Western Digital (NASDAQ:), along with technology sector peers Applied Materials (NASDAQ:), Lam Research (NASDAQ:) and KLA (NASDAQ:). Goldman Sachs analyst Mark Delaney explained: “We are now more positive on global memory stocks as we believe that the excess inventory memory companies are carrying will be depleted faster than our previous expectations, primarily in NAND flash as a result of the Toshiba Memory Corporation (TMC) fab outage that has disrupted a mid single digit percent of annual industry production (and to a lesser extent incremental capex/utilization cuts).” The industry’s underpinnings, Delaney believes, have set the stage for higher NAND prices through the third quarter. Delaney pointed to shrinking inventory levels and an accelerated depletion of inventories, “We believe that Micron is the best stock to express our view.” Arguably most important to current and would-be owners of MU stock, Delany notes, “…we believe that Micron’s stock will trade more on memory pricing trends and intermediate term EPS expectations than FY20 earnings.” If he’s right — and he likely is — the uptrend that took shape beginning in late June could indeed be the rekindled rebound effort by MU stock that first started to materialize early this year.

WD blamed that abrupt slowdown on the COVID-19 pandemic, and expects declining sales of its client devices (45% of its revenue last quarter) and data center devices (39% of its revenue) to wipe out higher sales of its client solutions (16% of its revenue).

articles.title: Seagate: A $30 Stock?
articles.content: Seagate’s Revenues could drop by over 30% from current levels of $10.5 billion to $7 billion by 2024, representing a compounded drop of roughly 10% per year (Seagate’s annual revenue has been hovering around $10-11 billion since FY 2016). We expect this trend to continue, and as retail demand is expected to drop even further, the drop in price per bit will easily outpace the rise in exabytes shipped, leading to a drop in revenues and margins. While we expect the share of enterprise storage in Seagate’s total revenue to keep rising, falling retail sales and a drop in net margins could see Seagate’s 30% revenue drop by 2024 translating into a roughly a 50% fall in EPS.

By Stephen Nellis Sept 17 (Reuters) - The newly appointed chief executive of SiFive Inc, a rising rival to Arm Ltd to supply chip designs, says Nvidia Corp's NVDA.O $40 billion agreement to acquire Arm has sparked fresh interest from customers about deepening ties with the young firm. Within hours of its announcement this week, the deal sparked worries in the chip industry that Nvidia would raise prices or otherwise make it harder for Nvidia's rivals to use Arm technology, despite a promise from both firms that Nvidia would keep Arm's neutral model.

articles.title: Why Western Digital Stock Just Jumped 11%
articles.content: What happened Shares of computer memory maker Western Digital Corporation (NASDAQ: WDC) are spinning higher Friday, up 10.8% as of 10 a.m. EST -- not due to any internet-inspired market manipulation, but because of a good old-fashioned earnings beat. Expected to report $0.54 per share in pro forma profit on sales of $3.9 billion, Western Digital nailed the revenue target in its fiscal second-quarter 2021 report released yesterday evening, and blew right past the earnings goal with $0.69 per share. Still, that was a whole lot better than the $0.47 per share Western Digital lost in the year-ago quarter -- and the company accomplished this despite its sales for the fiscal second quarter declining 7% year over year.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE-Samsung, SK Hynix to be spared brunt of China chip crackdown by U.S. -sources
articles.content: The Commerce Department, which plans to release new curbs on exports of technology to China this week, will likely deny requests by U.S. suppliers to send equipment to Chinese firms like Yangtze Memory Technologies Co Ltd (YMTC) and ChangXin Memory Technologies, Inc (CXMT) if they are making advanced DRAM or flash memory chips, the sources said. U.S. suppliers seeking to ship equipment to China-based semiconductor firms would not have to seek a license from the Commerce Department if selling to firms producing DRAM chips above the 18 nanometer node, NAND Flash chips below 128 layers, or logic chips above 14 nanometers, the sources said. However, U.S. companies selling sophisticated technology to indigenous Chinese chipmakers producing DRAM chips at 18 nanometers or below, NAND flash chips at or above 128 layers or logic chips at or under 14 nanometers would have to apply for a license that would be reviewed with the tough "presumption of denial" standard.

articles.title: Western Digital, Kioxia in advanced talks for merger - Bloomberg News
articles.content: Jan 20 (Reuters) - Memory chip maker Western Digital Corp WDC.O and Japan's Kioxia Holdings Corp are in advanced talks for a possible merger which will involve a dual-listing, Bloomberg News reported on Friday. In Japan, the two companies jointly produce NAND chips, which don't need power to retain data and are used in smartphones, TVs, data centre servers and public announcement display panels. Under the plan being discussed, Western Digital would spin off its flash business and merge it with Kioxia, creating a publicly traded company in the United States, Bloomberg said citing people familiar with the matter, adding that the company would also plan a second stock listing in Japan.

articles.title: Western Digital gets $900 million investment from Apollo, Elliot
articles.content: By Chibuike Oguh and Tiyashi Datta NEW YORK, Jan 31 (Reuters) - Memory chip maker Western Digital Corp WDC.O said on Tuesday it will receive $900 million through a convertible preferred stock deal from private equity firm Apollo Global Management Inc APO.N and hedge fund Elliott Management Corp. Western Digital said the preferred stock it sold to Apollo and Elliot has a conversion price of $47.75 per share, which is approximately a 9% premium on its closing price of $43.95 on Tuesday. On Tuesday, Western Digital CEO David Goeckeler said the partnership with Apollo and Elliott would help "facilitate the next stages of Western Digital's strategic review." Qatalyst Partners, Lazard and J.P. Morgan are serving as Western Digital’s financial advisers and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP is serving as Western Digital’s legal adviser.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE-Seagate settles with U.S. for shipping $1.1 bln of hard drives to Huawei
articles.content: By Karen Freifeld April 19 Reuters) - Seagate Technology Holdings STX.O has agreed to pay a $300 million penalty in a settlement with U.S. authorities for shipping over $1.1 billion worth of hard disk drives to China's Huawei in violation of U.S. export control laws, the U.S. Department of Commerce said on Wednesday. Seagate shipped 7.4 million drives to Huawei for about a year after the 2020 rule took effect and became Huawei's sole supplier of hard drives, the Commerce Department said. Even after "its competitors had stopped selling to them ... Seagate continued sending hard disk drives to Huawei," Matthew Axelrod, the Commerce Department's assistant secretary for export enforcement said in a statement.

articles.title: Seagate to pay $300 million penalty for shipping Huawei 7 million hard drives
articles.content: By Karen Freifeld April 19 Reuters) - Seagate Technology Holdings STX.O has agreed to pay a $300 million penalty in a settlement with U.S. authorities for shipping over $1.1 billion worth of hard disk drives to China's Huawei in violation of U.S. export control laws, the U.S. Department of Commerce said on Wednesday. Seagate sold the drives to Huawei between August 2020 and September 2021 despite an August 2020 rule that restricted sales of certain foreign items made with U.S. technology to the company. Seagate shipped 7.4 million drives to Huawei for about a year after the 2020 rule took effect and became Huawei's sole supplier of hard drives, the Commerce Department said.

articles.title: WDC Crosses Above Average Analyst Target
articles.content: And so with WDC crossing above that average target price of $50.83/share, investors in WDC have been given a good signal to spend fresh time assessing the company and deciding for themselves: is $50.83 just one stop on the way to an even higher target, or has the valuation gotten stretched to the point where it is time to think about taking some chips off the table? In recent trading, shares of Western Digital Corp (Symbol: WDC) have crossed above the average analyst 12-month target price of $50.83, changing hands for $51.15/share. But the whole reason to look at the average WDC price target in the first place is to tap into a "wisdom of crowds" effort, putting together the contributions of all the individual minds who contributed to the ultimate number, as opposed to what just one particular expert believes.
